title: How to tell if your laptop needs repair or replacement
metaDescription: A slow laptop isn't always a dead laptop. How to diagnose whether a repair is worth it — and when replacing it is the honest answer.
excerpt: A slow laptop isn't always a dead laptop. Here's how to diagnose whether a repair is worth it — and when replacing it is the honest answer.

body.text: A slow laptop is not automatically a broken laptop, and a broken laptop is not automatically a dead one. Most people bring a machine in expecting the worst, and most of the time it's a fixable problem — a failing drive, a clogged fan, or an operating system that just needs a clean install. If you're in East London and want a second opinion before you spend money on a new machine, [our IT support team](/troubleshoot) can diagnose it properly instead of guessing.

body.heading: Not sure which it is?
body.text: LYNX offers fixed-price diagnostics across the Eastern Cape. You'll know the cost before we touch anything.
Signs it's worth repairing
A repair makes sense when the cost is well under half the price of a comparable new machine, and when the rest of the hardware is still healthy.

items: **It's slow, not dead.** A sluggish machine with a working screen and keyboard is almost always a software or storage problem.
**The fan is loud or the laptop is hot.** That's dust and dried thermal paste — a cheap, fast fix that buys years.
**It won't boot, but the drive spins up.** Often a corrupted OS or a failing drive. Both are replaceable.
**The battery dies fast.** Batteries are consumables. Replacing one on a good laptop is almost always worth it.

body.text: Signs it's time to replace
Replacement is the honest answer when the repair cost starts approaching the price of something newer and faster.

items: **The motherboard has failed.** On older machines, motherboard replacement is often more expensive than the laptop is worth.
**The screen is cracked and the chassis is warped.** When two or three major components fail at once, you're rebuilding, not repairing.
**It's more than six or seven years old.** New low-end laptops now out-perform mid-range machines from a decade ago.
**It can't run the software you need.** Some hardware simply can't be upgraded to meet current requirements.

body.text: The honest rule of thumb

If the repair quote is under half the price of a comparable replacement, repair it. If it's over, replace it. If it's somewhere in between, it depends on how much you like the machine and how soon you'd want a new one anyway.

The one thing we'd always push back on is throwing a laptop away without a diagnosis. A fifteen-minute check-up costs a fraction of a new machine, and it's the only way to know which side of the line you're on. If you'd rather not guess, [see what a diagnostic visit covers](/troubleshoot) — or just [ask us directly](/contact).

title: Case Study: How Huddle solved the pickup sports admin nightmare
metaDescription: How we built Huddle, a React Native app that connects local sports players and eliminates the WhatsApp group chaos.
excerpt: Building a sports app isn't about the code. It's about solving the chaos of WhatsApp groups, dropped players, and last-minute cancellations. Here's how we built Huddle.

body.text: If you've ever tried to organise a casual game of basketball or football, you know the pain. Someone creates a WhatsApp group. Someone else suggests a time. People drop out. The location changes. Half the group doesn't see the message. By the time you actually play, you're exhausted from the admin, not the sport.

We built **Huddle** to fix this. It's a pickup sports discovery app that connects players with local games happening right now, taking the admin out of organising and putting the focus back on playing. You can [try the Beta here](https://joinhuddleup.netlify.app/).

body.heading: Want an app built?
body.text: LYNX doesn't just build for clients. We build our own products. If you have an idea that needs solving, let's talk.
The Problem

Before writing a single line of code, we interviewed local players in East London. The feedback was consistent: the admin was killing the fun. People wanted to play, but they didn't want to be the 'organiser' who had to chase 15 people for confirmation.
The Solution

We built Huddle using **React Native** for a single codebase that runs on both iOS and Android. The app uses localised discovery to show you games happening near you, complete with skill levels, player counts, and real-time confirmation. We added an anime/manga-inspired visual identity to break away from the sterile, corporate look of most fitness apps.
The Tech Stack

items: **Frontend:** React Native (iOS & Android)
**Backend:** Supabase for real-time database and auth
**Design:** Custom manga-inspired UI/UX

body.text: The Result

Huddle is currently live in Beta 1. The feedback has been incredible — players are finding games they never knew existed, and organisers are spending less time chasing confirmations and more time playing. This is the level of quality we bring to every client project at [LYNX Full-Stack](/fullstack).

title: Why your East London business needs a website (not just Facebook)

At [LYNX Full-Stack](/fullstack), we build websites for local businesses. Here is why a Facebook page alone isn't enough.

body.heading: Need a website?

1. Social media is rented land
If Facebook changes its algorithm tomorrow, your reach could drop to zero. If your account gets hacked or suspended, you lose contact with every customer. A website is yours. You control it.
2. Google doesn't rank Facebook pages

When someone in East London searches for 'plumber near me' or 'web designer East London', Google prioritises websites. Facebook pages are often buried. If you don't have a website, you're invisible to the most important search engine in the world.

A clean, well-designed website tells a customer that you are established and professional. It gives you a place to showcase your work, your team, and your story without being squeezed into a feed. Learn more about [why our clients choose us](/about).

A website lets you capture email addresses, run contact forms, and own the data. Social media platforms keep that data. When you own the channel, you build a long-term asset.

title: Practical AI for local businesses: What actually works in 2026
metaDescription: Stop worrying about AI taking over. Here is how small businesses in the Eastern Cape are using AI right now to save time and win more work.
excerpt: The AI hype cycle is exhausting. But there are genuinely useful, practical ways local businesses in East London are using AI right now to automate admin and save hours every week.

body.text: If you read the news, you'd think AI is either going to solve all our problems or end civilization. For a local business owner in East London, neither of those things is particularly useful. What's useful is knowing how to use AI to save an hour a day on admin.
Here is what's actually working for our clients right now.

body.heading: Ready for a tech upgrade?
body.text: We help local businesses figure out the right tools. Sometimes it's a simple automation, sometimes it's a custom web app.
1. Drafting emails and proposals

Tools like ChatGPT or Claude are surprisingly good at drafting the first version of a quote, a proposal, or a difficult email. It's not about letting the AI write it — it's about giving you a starting point to edit, which cuts writing time in half.
2. Customer service bots (that don't suck)

If your business gets the same 10 questions every day, a simple AI chatbot on your website can answer them. We build these using tools like Voiceflow or simple API integrations. It's not about replacing a human — it's about freeing up your receptionist to handle the complex questions.
3. Image editing

If you sell products online, AI photo editing tools (like removing backgrounds or enhancing lighting) can save hours on product photography. It's no longer necessary to hire a photographer for every single item.
4. Automating admin

Tools like Zapier or Make can connect your inbox to your CRM or spreadsheet. When a quote is accepted, it automatically creates an invoice. This is AI in the background, saving you time without you having to think about it.
What AI can't do
AI cannot replace a local relationship. It cannot shake a client's hand or fix a laptop. But it can give you back the time to do those things. That's the real value for a small business.

title: IT Support in East London: What Small Businesses Should Expect
metaDescription: A practical guide to IT support for East London businesses, from laptop and network repairs to remote help, clear pricing and ongoing support.
excerpt: From a failing laptop to unreliable Wi-Fi, here is what dependable IT support should look like for small businesses in East London.

body.text: When a laptop stops working, the office Wi-Fi drops, or the printer refuses to connect, a small business can lose hours. If your business operates in East London or the wider Eastern Cape, choosing the right [IT support partner](/troubleshoot) means knowing what can be fixed locally, what can be handled remotely, and what the service will cost.
Start with a clear diagnosis

Good support begins by understanding the symptoms, the equipment involved and how the problem affects your work. A technician should explain the likely cause, diagnostic steps and costs before carrying out chargeable work.
On-site help versus remote support

Hardware faults, damaged ports, cabling and certain printer issues may require an on-site visit in East London. Software configuration, account issues, updates and many connectivity checks can often be handled remotely across South Africa.

What determines the cost of a website?

items: Page count and content: original copy, photography and complex layouts take planning and production time.
Design requirements: tailored design takes more work than adapting a simple layout.
Functionality: forms, bookings, payments, accounts and searchable catalogues add complexity.
Integrations: connecting stock, accounting, CRM or third-party systems requires development and testing.
Ongoing needs: hosting, updates, backups, support and content changes should be considered separately.

A useful quote describes the deliverables, included pages, functionality, content responsibilities, revisions, recurring costs, ownership, timeline and post-launch support.

title: Remote vs On-Site IT Support: What Does Your Business Need?
metaDescription: Compare remote and on-site IT support for South African businesses. Learn which problems can be fixed remotely and when a technician needs to visit.
excerpt: Many IT problems can be diagnosed remotely, but hardware and physical network faults may need an on-site visit. Here is how to choose the right support.

body.text: The right choice between remote and on-site IT support depends on the fault, the equipment involved and whether someone needs to physically inspect or repair it. [LYNX Troubleshoot](/troubleshoot) helps businesses understand the next practical step.
What remote IT support can handle

items: Software installation and configuration.
Email, account and application troubleshooting.
Operating-system updates and performance checks.
Guidance with backups and basic security settings.
Initial diagnosis of some connectivity issues.

body.text: When an on-site visit makes more sense
A damaged laptop screen, faulty charging port, loose cable, failed router or printer hardware issue may require someone to examine the equipment directly.
Security and access matter

Remote support should be transparent and permission-based. You should know who is connecting, why access is needed and what the technician will do. Use trusted tools, avoid sharing passwords in plain text and end sessions when the work is complete.
